overview.title: SaaS Skeleton
overview.lead: The foundation for building multi-tenant CRM and ERP products. Sign-in, organizations, background jobs, files, live updates, notifications and the UI are already done — a new product starts straight from its own business logic.

about.title: What the product is
paragraphs: This is not a finished CRM but a skeleton you fork into a specific product. It has two separate parts: a workspace for customer organizations and an operator console used to onboard and support those organizations.

Each organization sees only its own data — the database itself guarantees this, not developer discipline. Customers and Calendar inside are working reference modules: a new section copies their structure instead of inventing its own.

goal.title: Main goal
paragraphs: A new domain module — tickets, billing, inventory — should take days, not weeks. Everything every SaaS repeats is solved once and the same way.
Key guarantees — organization isolation, an event only together with the saved fact, files bypassing the server — are built into the design, so a new module cannot “forget” them.

multitenancy.title: Multi-tenancy & RLS
business: One deployment, many customer organizations
Data is isolated per organization, not per user
Two independent portals: the organization's workspace and the operator console
technical: tenant_id + Postgres RLS as the main isolation mechanism
saas_migrator — schema owner (DDL)
saas_app — tenant runtime, RLS enforced
saas_platform — control plane, BYPASSRLS
Two independent planes with separate JWT secrets

messaging.title: Queue & transactional outbox
business: Background actions — emails, AI replies, notifications — never get lost
No duplicates, even on retry
Failed jobs are visible, not silently dropped
technical: publish(tx, …) inside the domain transaction
pg-boss queues are the outbox table
One queue per consumer: {message}/{consumer}
A shared DLQ across all consumers
Idempotency by messageId

realtime.title: Live updates
business: In-app notifications on business events without a page reload
Who is online right now
Delivered while the tab is open (no OS-level push yet)
technical: A Socket.IO gateway in every apps/api replica
Valkey (redis-streams-adapter) fans events out across all nodes
A browser on node A receives an event that happened on node B
No sticky sessions — the Docker Swarm VIP balances TCP
The worker delivers events through the same headless Socket.IO Server

auth.title: Authentication
business: Secure sign-in with short-lived sessions
Users see their devices and can end a session on any of them
A stolen session is detected and blocked automatically
Password recovery by email, and an admin can set a password directly
technical: Access token — a 15-minute JWT
Refresh token in an httpOnly cookie, rotated on every refresh
Reusing an old token revokes the session
Self-service “sign out everywhere”
A password reset (email or admin) revokes all sessions

files.title: File storage (S3)
business: Files can be attached to any business entity
Large uploads don't slow the app down
The storage provider can be swapped without code changes
technical: Any S3-compatible storage via environment variables
Self-hosted: SeaweedFS in dev (docker compose)
Cloud: AWS S3 — the same code, no rewrite
Two-phase presigned upload — the browser uploads directly, bypassing the API
Magic-byte type check, thumbnails, orphan cleanup cron

valkey.title: Valkey
business: Powers online presence and notification delivery
Can later double as an app cache — no new infrastructure
technical: Valkey 8 — a Redis-compatible fork, the same wire protocol
Used today for the Socket.IO adapter and presence leases
No caching layer yet
The same instance can serve as an app cache

i18n.title: Multi-language
business: The interface language stays in sync between the server and the frontend
A new market means new translations, not new code
technical: react-i18next on both frontends
The worker has its own i18next for emails
The backend returns codes, never text
English only for now
A TMS is deferred until the second language

infrastructure.title: Infrastructure
business: Runs on a single small server, no dedicated DevOps team
Self-hosted, no cloud vendor lock-in
technical: Dev: docker compose (Postgres, Mailpit, Valkey, SeaweedFS)
Prod: single-node Docker Swarm
6 images, 2 stacks (dev / prod)
GitLab CI → deploy via docker-context over SSH
